checkIns.summary: A live member asked directly (via chat, not the audit lane) why Legacy's contracts were so much more expensive on some nights, pointing at that night's real published book: MU $1020 CALL @ $24.88 ($2,488/contract) next to BMNR/ETHA/MARA at $52-$111/contract. Traced the root cause: pickChainContract (deterministic-edition.ts) picks the strike NEAREST TO SPOT (ATM) with no cost-awareness beyond the hard $35/share MAX_OPTION_PREMIUM_PER_SHARE ceiling -- that ceiling exists (PR-N15) only so a strong candidate is never dropped outright, never as an affordability target. Since ATM premium scales roughly linearly with the underlying's own price, the identical 'closest to spot' rule produces wildly different dollar costs across tickers purely as a function of stock price. Pulled MU's real live chain (spot $1017.75, Sep-25 expiry) to ground the fix: 0.50Delta ATM = $2,488/contract, 0.16Delta = $557/contract (still a real directional trade), sub-0.06Delta = $100-150/contract range (genuine lottery territory, not comparable to the other tickers' native cost). Shipped and merged PR #5344 same session: pickChainContract gained a strictly opt-in preferAffordable parameter -- when true, prefers the nearest-to-spot strike that ALSO clears premium <= $8/share AND |delta| >= 0.15, falling straight through to the exact unchanged ladder when nothing clears both (including when the row has no delta data at all, e.g. some UW-sourced rows). All 4 Legacy call sites (main synthesis loop, diversity-hedge swap, forced-contrarian re-score, buildRescuePlays) opted in; pickChainContract's other real caller, Vector (vector-play-candidates.ts/vector-dte-horizon.ts), is untouched by construction since it never passes the new parameter -- confirmed via Vector's own test suite passing unmodified.
checkIns.assessment: This is a genuine, member-facing product-quality fix, not a correctness bug -- every previously-published contract was legitimate and under the hard cap, just needlessly expensive on high-priced underlyings for no reason related to setup quality. The delta floor (0.15) is the load-bearing design choice: Swing's own HORIZONS config (horizons.ts) already documents having tried and reversed a pure cheap-OTM stance for exactly this reason (a 0.35Delta/[0.25,0.50] 'cheap OTM banger' policy was replaced with 0.50-0.75Delta because a multi-session thesis needs an instrument that tracks the underlying, not a low-delta lotto) -- reused that lesson rather than re-learning it. 7 new tests (regression proving default behavior unchanged, the preferred pick firing correctly, the delta floor correctly excluding a cheaper-but-too-low-delta strike, a no-delta-anywhere chain being a total no-op, an already-affordable ATM strike being unaffected, a no-gap-between-bars fallback case, and one full end-to-end buildDeterministicEditionPlays test). Full src/features/nighthawk/** suite: 1876/1876 pass. tsc clean, next lint clean. CI (verify + CodeQL) went green in ~7 minutes; merged via direct GitHub MCP merge_pull_request since automerge.yml's own merge step is known-broken per this file's own CLAUDE.md notes.

The reasoning is specific and falsifiable (real wall strikes, real gamma %, real distance-vs-expected-move math), not a generic catch-all excuse. checkIns.summary: Repeat-GREEN cycle on the healthcheck matrix (same MU/ETHA/MARA INVALIDATED + BMNR CONFIRMED state as 16:23Z/16:36Z/16:52Z) -- no new state transition. But traced the ROOT CAUSE of the gex-walls-veto escalation flagged at 16:23Z (knownOpenItems.gexWallsVetoRate_2026_09_21) while idle, and it is a real, high-confidence correctness finding, not just a magnitude WATCH item. src/lib/nighthawk/cortex/fetch.ts: vectorHorizonForCortexCommit(horizon: CortexCommitHorizon = '0dte') maps 'swing' -> Vector horizon 'monthly', everything else (including the default) -> '0dte'. The Legacy morning-confirm cron (src/app/api/cron/nighthawk-morning-confirm/route.ts:410) calls fetchCortexInputs(ps.ticker, direction, { now, timeoutMs: 4_000 }) with NO horizon option -- so it defaults to '0dte'. Repo-wide grep of every fetchCortexInputs(...) call site (morning-confirm, zerodte/exit-sync.ts, zerodte/cortex-gate.ts, bie/cortex-read.ts x2) found ZERO callers anywhere that pass horizon:'swing' -- the 'swing'->'monthly' branch is dead code, never exercised. Consequence: the shared gex-walls fresh-veto (src/lib/nighthawk/cortex/sources/gex-walls.ts, wallPathCheck, WALL_PATH_BLOCK_EM_FRAC=0.5) gates Legacy's multi-day-hold plays (DTE ~5-30 per the Legacy->Swing promotion window) against a SAME-DAY (0DTE) options-implied expected move, not one scaled to the play's actual holding horizon. A 0DTE expected move is dramatically narrower than a multi-day one (~sqrt(days) scaling -- a 10-day hold's real EM is roughly 3x a 0DTE EM), so 'target path crosses a dominant wall inside 0.5x expected move' fires far more readily than a correctly-scaled band would allow -- very likely the direct mechanical cause of today's 3-of-4 (75%) invalidation rate (MU/ETHA/MARA all cited this exact veto). For 0DTE's own commits (exit-sync.ts, cortex-gate.ts) the '0dte' default is CORRECT (0DTE literally trades same-day) -- this is not a bug there. It is specifically a Legacy-caller bug: the morning-confirm cron never opts into a horizon matching what it is actually gating.
checkIns.assessment: HIGH-CONFIDENCE, HIGH-PRIORITY finding -- but explicitly NOT fixing it myself this cycle. Two reasons: (1) it is a live-picks-gating-logic change (changes which Legacy plays get pre-open INVALIDATED), squarely inside this session's standing 'no scoring/ranking/gating changes without fresh explicit authorization' constraint and the Legacy mandate's own 'Ambiguous/live-picks-logic -> report, hold' escalation rule -- not a small/unambiguous CARVE-OUT fix. (2) the correct target horizon is itself a judgment call, not mechanical: 'swing'->'monthly' already exists and would be a large improvement over '0dte', but Legacy's real DTE floor (~5 days per the promotion-path gate) sits closer to VectorDteHorizon's 'weekly' option than 'monthly' for the shortest-dated plays -- picking between adding a genuine 'legacy' CortexCommitHorizon case (mapped to 'weekly' or 'monthly'), reusing the existing but never-yet-proven 'swing' case as-is, or scaling the EM lookup to the PLAY'S OWN per-ticket DTE rather than a fixed bucket, is a real design decision. Also worth flagging: the same default-0dte gap likely reaches Swing too (its own commit path was not traced this cycle -- out of this lane's scope -- but if Swing also never passes horizon:'swing', the identical mechanical bug would apply there).
